verdict.summary: The scheduler attempted the NewsStand heartbeat repeatedly on September 17 and 18 and logged generic 'Heartbeat automation did not complete' failures. The same desktop log records an account usage-limit response before the first failure, with a September 19 reset time. That is the strongest temporally matching cause, but the scheduled-run wrapper did not retain a nested per-run cause, and the database has no exact automation_runs rows for this automation. The existing heartbeat's prompt explicitly recovers overdue work at every later invocation. After capacity returned, the September 19 07:11 Vancouver invocation resumed the target thread and the current recovery produced a publicly verified service-plus-Weekly edition; foreground continuation means this is not proof of fully unattended recovery.

publicationOutcomes.backfillRule: Do not backdate newly written news; recover overdue work using current evidence and the actual publication date.

september19Recovery.scope: September 19 initial five service columns and recovered Weekly; zero new Daily news in this release
september19Recovery.limit: This proves recovery work can resume in the existing target after usage returns. Foreground coordination and user interaction mean it does not prove a fully unattended research-to-publication cycle.

priorTelemetry.relevance: Earlier telemetry already established that configuration and startup lines do not prove dispatch completion. The September 17-18 logs add explicit failures and an account usage-limit signal.

smallestConcreteFix.change: When a heartbeat receives an account usage-limit response, persist a typed FAILED_USAGE_LIMIT result for that due window and automatically requeue the same heartbeat once at or just after the supplied reset time. Preserve the original due phase in the retry metadata and continue using the existing target thread and overdue-work prompt.
smallestConcreteFix.whyThisIsSmallest: The existing schedule, target, and prompt are already correct. A second automation would duplicate production and still share the same account limit. Repository changes cannot make a model turn execute while the account is capped.
acceptance: One persisted run row binds automation ID, target thread, scheduled phase, trigger time, typed failure cause, retry time, and terminal result.
After a simulated or real usage-limit response, exactly one retry starts after reset without user input.
The retry begins with overdue recovery and does not backdate publication.
A future full scheduled source-to-publication cycle reaches public verification without foreground or user intervention.
smallestConcreteFix.currentAuthorizedAction: No automation mutation. Keep the single active heartbeat and observe the next due phase with exact trigger/result evidence.

irreducibleDependency: Available account model usage is required for the heartbeat to execute. If the cap recurs before runtime retry-after-reset exists, recovery waits for a later invocation or an explicitly authorized usage reset/new credit; no repository-only fix can remove that dependency.
